target_customer: Urban households and micro businesses in Colombia that pay for cleaning, later also companies
problem: Hiring reliable cleaners for homes was informal and inconsistent. Hogaru employs cleaners directly to raise retention and quality, unlike marketplaces.
business_model: Direct-employment cleaning services sold per service, with later payroll and affiliation services
product_category: Home and business cleaning services platform

founders.name: Gonzalo Ucar
founders.background_notes: Described by La Republica (2018) as one of two founders who lacked home help after moving to a new city.

founders.name: Matteo Cera
founders.background_notes: Named by La Republica in January 2018; not on the YC page.

founders.name: Oscar Pena
founders.background_notes: Named by La Republica in January 2018 as the engineer who co-founded; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Merger to expand across Colombia and Mexico, per press coverage; the YC directory still lists Hogaru as Active.

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking app plus operations; the hard parts were hiring, training and scheduling cleaners, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Direct employment gave quality control but any local cleaning firm could copy it; scale advantage came slowly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established cleaning firms faced digital competition from Hogaru per press; none acquired it.

market_need_then: Informal domestic work in Colombia and a regulated shift toward formal employment; La Republica reported 25,000 services per month and 560 formalised cleaners by January 2018.

branding.name_origin: Likely from the Spanish word hogar (home), but no source states the origin.
branding.domain_note: Uses hogaru.com; site footer shows Hogaru INC.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish language site, 'empresa lider en servicios de aseo'

branding.brand_signature: Directly employed cleaners with a Fairwork Kitemark shown on the site

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press (La Republica, Portafolio, Forbes Colombia, Bloomberg Linea) covered the brand repeatedly and it kept its own name after the 2023 merger.

outcome_analysis: Hogaru grew from a four person team in 2015 to hundreds of employees by 2019 and the YC page lists 746 team members. It merged with Homely in January 2023 to enter Mexico. Direct employment and demand for formal cleaning drove steady regional growth, though venture funding found was small.
notes: Seed of 810K USD in March 2017 comes from two aggregators (StartupIntros, Seedtable); investor list from Seedtable. Earlier angel round of 560K USD in June 2015 is on one aggregator only (Bouncewatch) and is unverified. Total raised varies by aggregator (1.11M to 1.37M USD). The merger with Homely is recorded as an exit of type merger even though the directory status is Active, because both entities continue. Competitors named in press were not tied to dates at or near 2017, so the list is empty. Founder education and employers not found.
